review: 1:2 כִּסֵּא רַחֲמָיו — the Arabic كُرْسِيُّ رَحْمَتِه is the 'mercy seat'; Hebrew keeps כִּסֵּא with the suffix, since כַּפֹּרֶת would name the lid rather than the throne.
2:3–2:4 אֶקְרַב וְאֶתְבַּע / אֶת־הַבְטָחָתְךָ — 'I draw near and claim Your promise'; the Arabic مُطَالِبًا is a participle of demand, which Hebrew turns into a finite verb for the rhyme with 2:4.
3:1–3:2 הֱיֵה מָגֵן / וּמִשְׂגָּב עֹז — two psalmic titles (Ps 3:4, Ps 9:10); the Arabic تُرْسًا ... وَمَلْجَأً حَصِينًا is the same pair.
3:3 טַעֲנָתִי נֶגֶד — 'my plea against' the accuser; נֶגֶד is left without an object because the accuser is supplied by the next clause in Arabic, and the line would otherwise run long.
4:1 תַּדְהִימֵנִי — 'astonishes me'; the biblical verb is תָּמַהּ, but the hiph'il of דהם is the liturgical form used for يُدْهِش.
